Design a modern, luxury resort website inspired by lakeside resorts in Ghana.
The website should visually match the resort brand by extracting or matching colors from the following inspiration sources (videos and pages provided by the user). Use earthy, natural, and relaxing tones such as lake blues, forest greens, warm browns, soft golds, and sunset accents. Make it Ghana friendly 
Pages & Sections:
1.	Hero Section
o	Full-screen video or image slider showing the lake, rooms, and nature
o	Animated headline text (fade-in + slide-up)
o	Call-to-action buttons:
	“Book a Room”
	“Call to Book”
2.	About the Resort
o	Smooth text reveal animations
o	Short story describing the peaceful lakeside experience
3.	Rooms & Pricing
o	Card-based layout for room listings
o	Each room card includes:
	Image carousel (with smooth transitions)
	Room name
	Price per night
	Short description
	“Book Now” button
o	Hover animations on cards (scale, shadow, soft glow)
4.	Gallery / Location Experience
o	Masonry or grid gallery layout
o	Scroll-triggered animations for images
o	Lightbox image preview
5.	Amenities
o	Icons with subtle motion animations
o	Examples: lake view, restaurant, boat rides, relaxation areas
6.	Booking Section
o	Booking form UI with:
	Check-in & check-out dates
	Room type selection
	Number of guests
	Submit button
o	Show price estimate dynamically
7.	Contact Section
o	Click-to-call phone number
o	WhatsApp booking button
o	Embedded Google Map
8.	Footer
o	Social media links
o	Address
o	Copyright
Animations & Motion:
•	Use smooth page transitions
•	Text fade-in, slide-up, and staggered animations
•	Image zoom-on-scroll effects
•	Floating buttons with gentle motion
Design Style:
•	Clean, premium, resort-style layout
•	Large typography
•	Rounded cards
•	Soft shadows
•	Mobile-first responsive design
Tech Preferences:
•	Frontend framework: React / Next.js
•	Styling: Tailwind CSS
•	Animations: Framer Motion or GSAP
Make the site feel calm, luxurious, and vacation-ready, encouraging users to book or call immediately.

**Conceptualizing The Site**

I'm currently fleshing out the core concepts for this Ghanaian lakeside resort website. The plan is to capture that luxurious, yet earthy feel. I'm focusing on bringing the desired color palette into the web design, especially the lake blue, forest green, and the warm brown earthy tones. My main goal is to represent a premium vacation experience.


**Define the Framework**

I've sketched out the application's skeletal structure. I'm leveraging React 18 with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS to build the components efficiently. I've broken it into distinct sections: Hero, About, Rooms, Gallery, Amenities, Booking, Contact, and Footer. Also using Lucide React for crisp icons and Framer Motion for appealing animations. It will include animated headlines, hover effects, a masonry gallery, dynamic price estimation, and a mobile-first design.


**Developing Visual Language**

I'm now nailing down the color palette in the Tailwind config. Primary forest green and secondary gold tones are defined. Accent lake blue is set, and background and text colors are chosen. For typography, serif headings convey luxury while sans-serif body text keeps things readable. This allows for styling adjustments like tracking and weight.


**Adding Component Logic**

I'm now integrating the logic for the Amenities, Booking, and Contact components. I've chosen Lucide icons for Amenities and added a staggered animation for a dynamic feel. For Booking, I'm using state management for dates, room types, and guests to enable price estimation. The Contact section uses a Google Maps embed for location and a WhatsApp link for direct communication.


**Refining Component Interactions**

I'm currently working on the Gallery component, implementing a lightbox effect via a simple overlay state to enhance the user experience. I've ensured mobile responsiveness by using Tailwind classes to control image widths across different screen sizes. My focus is on writing the code efficiently, keeping styles inline with Tailwind to avoid external CSS files and integrating placeholder images for quick iteration. I've laid the groundwork for the main application structure, including the initial boilerplate and core components such as Hero, Rooms, and Booking sections. I'm exploring Framer Motion for Rooms' carousel, aiming for premium visuals without sacrificing performance. The Booking form is coming together, styled with Tailwind to give a premium feel.


**Verifying TypeScript Usage**

I'm now focusing on TypeScript compliance and ensuring clean imports. I've checked for proper `createRoot` usage and verified the specific color requests: `bg-emerald-950` for forest green, `text-amber-600` for gold/sunset, `bg-stone-100` for sand/brown, and `text-teal-800` for lake blue, matching the earlier specified color scheme. I'm nearly ready to output the final XML block now.
